speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the exact location of your pain and whether it has migrated to your right lower quadrant. Additionally, have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or fever since the onset?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mesenteric Ischemia. Given your recent heart attack, the sudden abdominal pain, and bloody stools, this is likely an intestinal blockage due to poor blood flow. Do you have a history of atrial fibrillation or peripheral artery disease? REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of the Abdomen. REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Abdomen_Angio.
